messages.author: 9ec69ca07f36d6a1
messages.subject: Overly wide figures and justification
parts:
When I instruct knitr to use a floating figure and the figure is too wide, it will jut out into the right margin, but even though I default to centering figures, these too-large figures will not jut out a bit into the left margin in an attempt to better center the image.

Any advice appreciated
Thanks
Frank

messages.author: 9ec69ca07f36d6a1
messages.subject: Re: Overly wide figures and justification
parts:
I see from a LaTeX online discussion that swapping \centerline{ } for \centering will make this work.  Is there an easy way to tell knitr to use \centerline instead of the default when generating the \includegraphics{}?

Thanks
Frank

messages.subject: Re: [knitr] Re: Overly wide figures and justification
parts:
Hi Frank,

I believe this will just require writing a custom hook.  Hooks handle this output formatting, and are specific to the output device. Just copy and paste the hook code definition from https://github.com/yihui/knitr/blob/master/R/hooks-latex.R into a custom hook, swapping out the "centering" command.  Oh ha, it looks like you answered your own question while I write this.  Um, hooks: http://yihui.name/knitr/hooks are already defined to make customization easier, though your use of centerline{} sounds like a good one.  I guess for some reason it's not possible/desirable to just generate a smaller plot that won't overflow in the first place in your case?

messages.author: cc1ef8c8158d6b73
messages.subject: Re: [knitr] Re: Overly wide figures and justification
parts:
In this particular case, I think a quick gsub() should solve the problem, e.g.

\documentclass{article}
\begin{document}
<<setup, include=FALSE>>=
hook_chunk = knit_hooks$get('chunk')
knit_hooks$set(chunk = function(x, options) {
res = hook_chunk(x, options)
if (options$fig.align != 'center') return(res)
gsub('\\{\\\\centering (\\\\includegraphics.+)\n\n\\}',
'\\\\centerline{\\1}', res)
})
@

<<test, fig.height=4, fig.width=8, out.width='6in', fig.align='center'>>=
par(mar=c(4,4,.1,.1))
plot(mpg~wt, data=mtcars)
@
\end{document}

This is hackish, of course. You are recommended to put Rnw and tex
output under version control, so you will be aware of the possible
future changes.

Regards,
Yihui
